payload.title: File:Ceratopsidae Scale.svg
payload.description_html:
Size comparison of several members of Ceratopsidae. The taxa included are listed here (from left to right): Left side: Nasutoceratops titusi, Styracosaurus albertensis, Centrosaurus apertus, and Pachyrhinosaurus canadensis. Right side: Triceratops prorsus, Pentaceratops sternbergii, Chasmosaurus belli, and Anchiceratops ornatus. The human silhouette is from File:Silhouette of man standing and facing forward.svg (CC0).
  • Nasutoceratops
    • Sampson, S.D.; Lund, E.K.; Loewen, M.A.; Farke, A.A.; Clayton, K.E. (2013). "A remarkable short-snouted horned dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (late Campanian) of southern Laramidia". Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences 280 (1766): 20131186.
  • Styracosaurus: see File:Styracosaurus Scale.svg for details
  • Centrosaurus: see File:Centrosaurus Scale.svg for details
  • Pachyrhinosaurus: see File:Pachyrhinosaurus Scale 2.svg for details
  • Triceratops
    • See File:Triceratops Scale V1.svg for details, note that postcranium is based on T. horridus
    • Skull size matches that given in:
      • Scannella, J.B.; Horner, J.R. (2010). "Torosaurus Marsh, 1891, is Triceratops Marsh, 1889 (Ceratopsidae: Chasmosaurinae): Synonymy through ontogeny". Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology 30 (4): 1157-1168.
    • Horn shape based on:
      • Witton, M.P. (2018) The Palaeoartist's Handbook, The Crowood Press
  • Pentaceratops: see File:Pentaceratops Size.svg for details
  • Chasmosaurus
    • Skeletal diagram by Scott Hartman
    • Godfrey, S.J.; Holmes, R. (1995). "Cranial morphology and systematics of Chasmosaurus (Dinosauria: Ceratopsidae) from the Upper Cretaceous of western Canada". Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology 15 (4): 726-742.
  • Anchiceratops: see File:Anchiceratops Size.svg for details
